rule: Run free oblivion jobs serially — never run a heavy consumer (e.g. atom-build) concurrently with another heavy consumer (e.g. the k-replicate scorer) against the single shared vLLM instance, since the loser is starved and silently yields near-zero output.
check: A flock-based mutex wrapper-script around the known heavy-job launchers (atom-build, scorer) that serializes access to the oblivion endpoint
misses: Any new/future heavy consumer not wrapped, or a job launched ad hoc (manual curl, one-off script) that bypasses the wrapper entirely; also can't detect starvation after the fact, only prevent the specific known collision

rule: Cite the FM-n identifiers from the canonical ~/projects/fleet/orchestration/FAILURE-MODES.md and fleet/CODING-INVARIANTS.md when auditing or briefing orchestration code, not this memory file, which is a recognition-only pointer.

Before presenting any ratio or normalized score built from two sample-size-dependent statistics, explicitly check N-invariance (recompute at multiple N or derive scaling analytically) rather than assuming the ratio is scale-invariant.

A coordinator must execute founder-authorized destructive/irreversible steps itself rather than relaying "the founder approved X" to a subagent, since a subagent cannot verify a relayed authorization claim and must treat it as untrusted.

To test whether X causes a failure, remove X and confirm the removal took effect before retesting, rather than relying on a flag or env var believed (but unverified) to bypass X, and never upgrade an unvalidated control's negative result into a conclusion.

A registry of ten repo-maintenance triage failure modes (stale CI read as verdict, green-but-stale-base merges, duplicate dispatch, git --all footguns, stale handoff state, rebase/force-push gating, unparseable-workflow invisibility, worktree-log loss, live shared-checkout collisions) with per-FM how-to-apply guidance.
check: GitHub branch-protection "require branches to be up to date before merging" (covers FM-2) plus an actionlint CI job on workflow files (covers FM-8)
misses: FM-1 (stale-CI-timestamp comparison), FM-3 (duplicate dispatch on the same work item), FM-4 (git log --all ref footgun), FM-5 (stale handoff vs live gh state), FM-6 (rebase vs merge choice), FM-9 (worktree log loss on cleanup), FM-10 (detecting a live concurrent session in a shared checkout) all require situational judgment with no generic deterministic check

rule: When a tool reports an auth/connectivity/state failure, run that tool's own status or list subcommand before theorizing from its config files, since config reflects intent while the status command reflects current runtime/credential state.

When retiring a git checkout overlaid on a shared/home directory, bundle the full history first, then remove only tracked files (git ls-files) rather than rm -rf, pass two safety gates (no tracked file under a personal path; known personal tools untracked) with pasted command output, and get founder confirmation before the irreversible wipe step.
check: A wrapper-script running the two named safety-gate commands (`git ls-files | grep -E '^(\.claude|projects|Documents|\.ssh|\.gnupg|\.config)/'` must be empty; `git ls-files --error-unmatch <known-personal-tool>` must fail) and aborting the wipe if either fails
misses: Personal paths/tools not in the hardcoded pattern list, the requirement to actually paste gate output into the report (vs claiming it passed), and the founder-confirmation step itself, which is a judgment/authorization gate not a mechanical one

rule: Any self-observing/autonomous subsystem must alarm on empty-or-all-reject output, never coerce a dependency/transport error into a substantive verdict, health-check backends after any migration, never hardcode a success field, avoid dedup keys that can never collide, and avoid learning from its own test runs rather than founder actions.

Before retiring or moving a shared/junk-drawer .git, enumerate what it actually backs (git branch -vv, git worktree list, git stash list) and confirm which project each branch belongs to before writing to or removing anything, since one .git can back many unrelated projects' unpushed work.
check: A wrapper-script that runs the three enumeration commands and refuses to proceed to the destructive removal step unless their output has been reviewed (non-empty results block auto-proceed)
misses: Correctly interpreting which branch belongs to which project (matching remote URL / CLAUDE.md frontmatter to intent) is a judgment call the script cannot make on its own

rule: For remote/fleet AI implementers, delegate only fully-specified diff application (coordinator authors the literal diff and verifies it, fleet applies it mechanically on a fresh branch) rather than open-ended "fix this bug" briefs, which empirically fail far more often.

Never use `git merge-base --is-ancestor` as the safety gate for whether it's safe to delete a worktree or branch, since squash-merges make it report NOT-MERGED for every already-merged branch; gate worktree/branch removal instead on PR state (gh pr view --json state,mergedAt) and, load-bearingly, on `git status --porcelain` being empty before removal.
check: A cleanup wrapper-script that runs `git status --porcelain` and aborts the `git worktree remove`/branch-delete step if it is non-empty, using `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` (not `--is-ancestor`) to determine merge status
